title: Debt Crisis Explodes: France Is Burning—What’s Next? | Matthew Piepenburg
speaker: Matthew Piepenburg (guest, Von Greyerz)

macro_themes.view: The US and France (120%+ debt/GDP, rising yields) are already in a debt crisis; debt crises lead to currency debasement, inflation and social unrest.
Yields have not peaked unless central banks cap them via yield curve control/money printing, which would debase the currency.
True inflation is near 10%, so even 7% bond yields are negative in real terms; governments must inflate away debt.

macro_themes.theme: AI bubble and AI credit risk
macro_themes.view: AI capex is the worst misallocation of capital in history; CoreWeave-type debt stress will become the rule and could drag the S&P, Dow and Nasdaq down within 2-3 years.

macro_themes.theme: Rotation from tech stocks into bonds
macro_themes.view: Below-par high-coupon corporate bonds (e.g. Apple) are drawing money out of stocks; signals the end of a credit cycle.
Expect more yield curve control/Operation Twist, QE, possibly a gold-backed bond, gold revaluation, stablecoin push, even restructuring; none will fix the debt.
Dollar will be repriced and debased in a more multipolar world; central banks keep stacking gold.

calls.reason: Debt too high to grow out of, so governments will debase currencies and run negative real rates; gold outperforms stocks and bonds measured in real terms.
calls.quote: that yield, which makes gold so unattractive, is actually no yield at all. And gold is outperforming the very currency

calls.condition: Unless the Fed/Treasury caps yields with yield curve control or money printing.
calls.reason: Weak demand for Treasuries (China, Japan selling) and unsustainable issuance mean yields have not peaked.
calls.quote: Have bond yields peaked is my question. >> No, not at all. Unless there's unless you use yield curve control

calls.condition: If AI productivity assumptions prove wrong (his base case), over roughly a 2-3 year window.
calls.reason: S&P is concentrated in overvalued, debt-funded AI hyperscalers; AI overinvestment is the worst capital misallocation ever.
calls.quote: they take the entire S&P, Dow, and NASDAQ with them

calls.reason: Over $50B of debt, CDS at distress levels, insiders selling; a canary for AI credit risk.
calls.quote: you couldn't get me to sell those bonds fast enough if I held them right now and to get out of those stocks fast enough

calls.reason: Debt must be inflated away; expects a repriced, debased dollar and less dollar hegemony.
calls.quote: It just means a repricing of the dollar, less dollar hedgeimonyy

notes: Guest is a gold dealer (self-declared sell-side bias). US 10y 5.14 was quoted by the host. ES call is long-horizon and conditional on AI thesis failing. He calls below-par Apple bonds a 'nice safe bet' (bonds, not stock; not recorded). Video date from listing; protests were 'over the weekend'.
